description: Small Ralph self-iteration focused first on fresh CI health for the current main/branch tip, then two verifiable follow-up repairs from the web CI and dogfood surfaces. The goal is to keep OSv2 service and upper-layer experience work shippable by removing deterministic CI blockers before adding broader capability work.

userStories.name: Make Go lint CI compatible with Go 1.25
userStories.description: The latest GitHub CI run fails in the Go job before linting because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins `golangci-lint-action` to v2.1.6 while `go.mod` targets Go 1.25.0. The downloaded v2.1.6 binary was built with Go 1.24, which golangci-lint rejects for a Go 1.25 target. Pin CI to a golangci-lint release that officially supports Go 1.25, keep lint as a new-issues ratchet while inherited findings remain, and guard the workflow against regressing to an incompatible version.
bdd_acceptance: Given `go.mod` targets Go 1.25.0, When the CI workflow is checked, Then the golangci-lint action version is at least v2.4.0.
Given the workflow uses the official golangci-lint action, When maintainers review CI config, Then the action remains pinned to an explicit release instead of a floating tag.

Given the repository currently has inherited lint findings, When the CI workflow is checked, Then the golangci-lint action runs with `only-new-issues: true` so branch CI gates new lint debt without failing every historical finding.
Given a future change lowers the action version below the Go 1.25 support floor, When the repository tests run, Then a BDD guard test fails with a message naming the minimum compatible version.
ci_evidence: GitHub CI run 26017200976 on 2026-05-18 failed in Go / golangci-lint with: `the Go language version (go1.24) used to build golangci-lint is lower than the targeted Go version (1.25.0)`.
Official golangci-lint FAQ says golangci-lint supports Go versions lower than or equal to the Go version used to compile the binary.
Official golangci-lint Go 1.25 issue says support starts at v2.4.0 when compiled with Go 1.25 and official binaries are built with Go 1.25.
Red on 2026-05-18: `go test ./scripts/ci -run TestBDD_GolangCILintWorkflowSupportsGo125 -count=1 -v` failed because CI pinned v2.1.6.

Additional root-cause evidence on 2026-05-18: `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4 run --timeout=5m` loaded the config but reported 1220 inherited lint findings, so the CI repair needs a new-issues ratchet.
Red on 2026-05-18: after adding the ratchet guard, `go test ./scripts/ci -run TestBDD_GolangCILintWorkflowSupportsGo125 -count=1 -v` failed because `only-new-issues` was absent.
Green on 2026-05-18: `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.11.4 run --timeout=5m --new-from-rev=HEAD` reported `0 issues`.
quality_gates: Red BDD guard for CI golangci-lint version compatibility.

userStories.name: Stabilize US-453 compliance downloads in full Vitest coverage
userStories.description: The latest GitHub web CI still fails during the full `npx vitest run --coverage` job in the US-453 compliance report spec. Local targeted non-coverage execution passes, so the repair should root-cause the full-suite or coverage-only interaction and keep binary/JSON download behavior stable.
bdd_acceptance: Given the compliance report spec runs under Vitest coverage, When the SOC2 JSON path downloads the response, Then exactly one download record is captured with a `.json` filename.
Given streamless binary responses in jsdom, When PDF or GDPR ZIP downloads run, Then `object.stream is not a function` is hidden by the fallback attachment reader.
Given the full web test suite runs with coverage, When US-453 executes after neighboring specs, Then its download mocks remain isolated from prior tests.
Targeted and full relevant web tests pass.
ci_evidence: GitHub CI run 26017200976 failed in Web / Vitest with coverage at `ComplianceReportsPage.test.tsx:217`, expecting one JSON download but receiving zero.
Local targeted run without coverage on 2026-05-18 passed: `cd web && npx vitest run src/components/admin/__tests__/ComplianceReportsPage.test.tsx --coverage=false`.
Search confirmed the known `object.stream is not a function` case is modeled in `ComplianceReportsPage.test.tsx` via `streamlessBinaryResponse`.
quality_gates: Red reproduction for US-453 under coverage or full-suite ordering.

userStories.name: Repair Northwind E2E seed wipe ordering
userStories.description: The 2026-05-17 WebUI dogfood report found that `scripts/e2e-setup.sh` leaves the Northwind explorer empty because the seed wipe hits a `functions_ontology_rid_fkey` foreign-key violation. Fix the seed/reset ordering so the OSv2 browser and Explorer dogfood paths have a populated Northwind ontology.
bdd_acceptance: Given an existing seeded database with functions attached to an ontology, When `scripts/e2e-setup.sh` resets Northwind data, Then the wipe deletes or detaches dependent rows before ontology rows.
Given the seed completes, When `/api/v2/ontologies/northwind/objectTypes` is queried, Then it returns expected object types such as Customers, Orders, or Products.
Given the seed script fails, When it exits, Then the error names the failed seed phase and keeps enough output for CI diagnosis.
Targeted seed/reset tests or a local e2e seed smoke pass.
ci_evidence: Dogfood report `dogfood-output/weave-webui-dogfood-20260517.md` records DOG-001: `scripts/e2e-setup.sh` fails during seed wipe with `functions_ontology_rid_fkey` and `/explorer/northwind` renders `No object types`.
The same report records no persistent browser JS errors across sampled routes, making seed data health the blocker for Northwind Explorer confidence.
quality_gates: Red seed wipe regression test or reproducible local seed failure.
Targeted seed/reset test or smoke command selected during implementation.
